summary: Iteration 6 — full validation of the new 4-tier subscription system (free/plus/pro/yearly). Created /app/backend/tests/test_subscriptions.py with 23 focused pytest cases covering: /api/subscription/tiers shape & prices (£0/£14.99/£24.99/£239.99 + BEST VALUE on yearly), /api/subscription/checkout for plus/pro/yearly all returning real Stripe checkout_url (host stripe.com), unknown plan rejected (422/400), /api/subscription/portal 400 without stripe_customer_id, /api/subscription/usage shape, new-signup → tier='trial_pro' with 13–14 trial_days_remaining, trial_pro CAN call /api/lex/practice (no 402), free user 402 with correct tier name in detail on practice/live-assist/contracts/voice/court_categories/premium templates, free-user /api/lex/chat quota = 5 daily then 429, free-user /api/letters/generate quota = 1 monthly then 429, plus user can practice but live-assist 402 (mentions Pro), pro user can call live-assist and witness_statement premium template, PRICE_TO_TIER mapping constants verified, and regression checks that /api/emergency/rights and /api/lawfirms STILL work for free users. Result: 23/23 PASSED after 2 backend fixes were applied. Frontend (mobile 390x844, trial_pro user): trial banner correctly reads '13 days left in free trial (Pro features unlocked)' ✓, no lock badges (🔒) shown ✓, Subscribe modal opens via Settings → Change plan, contains all 4 tier-card-{free|plus|pro|yearly} cards ✓, BEST VALUE badge ✓, YOUR PLAN badge ✓, prices £14.99/£24.99/£239.99 visible (Free card shows 'Free' rather than literal '£0'). Settings modal shows settings-subscription card ✓, settings-contact card with 4 contact-* mailto links (admin/press/support/info) ✓, and settings-trustpilot link ✓.

critical.issue: CheckoutRequest.plan was typed Literal['monthly','yearly'] — sending plan='plus' or plan='pro' returned 422 (Pydantic), never reaching the endpoint logic that already maps plus/pro/yearly to the correct Stripe price IDs. FIXED in this iteration by widening the Literal to ['plus','pro','yearly','monthly']. Without this fix, the Subscribe modal's Plus & Pro buttons would have failed in production.

TIER_QUOTAS used keys 'letters_monthly' and 'evidence_monthly' but check_quota_and_increment built the lookup key as f'{feature}_{period}' producing 'letters_generate_monthly' / 'evidence_analyze_monthly' — those keys did NOT exist in TIER_QUOTAS, so the lookup returned None (unlimited). Free-tier users would have had UNLIMITED letter generation and unlimited evidence analyses, contradicting the documented 1/month quota. FIXED by renaming TIER_QUOTAS keys to match feature names and updating get_user_usage_summary accordingly.

minor.issue: Unknown plan returns 422 (Pydantic Literal error) not 400 as the review request expected. Behavior is still 'client error' but the response shape is Pydantic's validation envelope, not the hand-written {detail:'Unknown plan ...'} message. Consider switching to a free-form str + manual 400 raise for a cleaner API contract.
PRICE_TO_TIER mapping logic verified statically (constants are correct). Could not execute a signed live webhook test from outside; recommend a Stripe CLI replay test before launch.

ui_bugs.issue: Free tier price displays as the word 'Free' rather than the literal '£0' specified in the review request. Minor — header line shows 'Free Free' (name + price column). Consider unifying to '£0/forever' for consistency with the other 3 cards.

issues: Modal content is tall; Subscribe button sits below the fold on first open — user must scroll inside the modal to reach the CTA. Same pattern as previously-reported Terms modal.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1694 lines — strongly recommend splitting into /routers (auth, lex, letters, subscription, webhooks) and /core (tier_gate, quota, prompts) before adding more tiers/features. The PRICE_TO_TIER constant is at line 49 but referenced both by /checkout and by /webhook/stripe ~1.2k lines later — splitting will reduce regression risk.

TIER_QUOTAS / FEATURE_MIN_TIER / TIER_ORDER are three parallel dicts keyed by tier and feature — easy to drift out of sync (already happened: see the letters_monthly/evidence_monthly bug fixed this iteration). Refactor to a single source of truth: e.g., a TIER_SPEC = {'free': {'min_tier_for': {...}, 'quotas': {...}}, ...} or an enum class.

check_quota_and_increment increments the counter BEFORE the AI call. If the LLM throws and the endpoint returns 500, the user's quota is still burned. Consider decrement-on-failure or check-then-increment-after-success.

/api/subscription/activate-test endpoint is still exposed in production (line 1140) — any authenticated user can set tier='pro' / 'yearly' on themselves without paying. Gate behind an env flag (e.g., ENABLE_TEST_HOOKS=1) before launch.

Stripe webhook handler accepts unverified payloads when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty — currently the secret IS set, but the fallback path remains and only emits a warning. Make missing secret a hard fail (HTTPException 503) outside of explicit dev mode.

user_to_public infers tier on every call from trial_end_date + sub_status. Cheap, but means the persisted user.tier field can disagree with the computed tier (e.g., a user with tier='plus' in db but expired trial AND no active subscription will show as 'free'). Acceptable but document the precedence rule.

Frontend SubscribeModal shows the same Pro highlights for both 'pro' and 'yearly' but the yearly card highlights only mention 'Save 20%' — the visible feature list under yearly may look thin; consider inheriting Pro highlights + appending savings.

rca of the issue: BUG 1 (checkout 422 on plus/pro): CheckoutRequest model carried over from the legacy 2-tier (monthly/yearly) implementation; when the endpoint body was upgraded to handle 'plus'/'pro'/'yearly' via a dict lookup, the Pydantic Literal type was not widened, so all plus/pro requests were rejected at the schema layer before the dict lookup could run. Reproduction: POST /api/subscription/checkout with {"plan":"plus"} → 422 literal_error. Fix: widened Literal to ['plus','pro','yearly','monthly']. BUG 2 (free quotas never enforced for letters/evidence): TIER_QUOTAS dict used short keys (letters_monthly, evidence_monthly) while check_quota_and_increment built keys via f'{feature}_{period}' where feature='letters_generate' / 'evidence_analyze' — producing keys that do not exist in TIER_QUOTAS, so .get() returned None (= unlimited). Reproduction: free user calls /api/letters/generate twice in the same month → both return 200 (expected: 2nd = 429). Fix: renamed TIER_QUOTAS keys to letters_generate_monthly + evidence_analyze_monthly and updated get_user_usage_summary's tuple to match. Both fixes verified by re-running the failing tests — now PASS.
